$comment: DRAFT FOR CR-857 -- lives in studies/ until CR-857 lands it under docs/development-rules/ (JDG-3414, JDG-3420). Validates docs/spec/_source/glossary.json, the names dictionary and the single source of truth for every name (JDG-3411, JDG-3419). English is the primary text and Japanese its translation (JDG-3422). Order is array position only (JDG-3423).
title: The names dictionary manuscript
description: Every name GRS uses: data entities, properties, screen parts, setting keys, Agent API members, document commands and the value words. Each term is keyed by the name itself; a key whose meaning changes with its owner gets one term per owner, with the owner in its own field (JDG-3415; OMPV keeps the key and the owner apart). The glossary table, the schema descriptions and the MCP descriptions are generated from this file in one step (JDG-3416).

groups.description: The top of the taxonomy. The order of the groups is the order of the generated glossary and of the parts of the review sheet.

Text.description: One text per language, one language per property (OKPN/OMPV: never two languages in one string). en is the primary text; ja translates it; more languages may be added as further language tags.

Key.description: A name as code writes it: start, Task, taskGroupLane.

TermRef.description: Points at one term: its key, and its owner when the term has one.

key.description: The name itself. The pair (key, owner) is unique across the whole dictionary, children included.

owner.description: The entity or part that owns the key, given only when the key means different things under different owners (kind under Color).

rowId.description: The specification row that cites this term today (N-1, PR-1, IC-7), kept so that existing references still resolve.

since.description: For a term of a contract group (GRS JSON, Agent API, document commands): the schemaVersion or agentApiVersion that first published it. A published term never changes its name or meaning.

label.description: The name a person sees. Omit it when the person sees the key itself (a JSON key, an API member).

definition.description: What the term means. The schema and MCP descriptions take the English text.

nonLiteral.description: Why the Japanese label is not a literal translation of the English one. Present only for the few agreed exceptions.

avoid.description: Words that must not stand in for this term.

uses.description: Where the generators print this term. Whether each place really uses it is checked, not trusted.

tags.description: Related terms. Every one must exist in the dictionary.

children.description: Terms derived from this one, in reading order.
